evidence.excerpt: A commercial Corynebacterium glutamicum strain used in lysine production was revived from glycerol stocks stored at −80°C for periods of 1, 3, 5, and 8 years. After standardised revival and single-passage propagation, 200 colonies per stock age were characterised for growth rate on minimal medium, lysine secretion by HPLC, and cell morphology. Coefficient of variation in lysine titre per colony increased from 9% (1-year stocks) to 24% (8-year stocks). Mean titre per colony decreased by 11% over 8 years. Whole-genome sequencing of three low-titre and three high-titre colonies from each cohort identified no fixed mutations but showed varying proportions of a frameshift variant in the lysC gene encoding aspartate kinase. The finding indicates that long storage does not eliminate heterogeneity and that periodic single-colony isolation for stock renewal is warranted at intervals shorter than 5 years.
